key_insight: SHERLOC reframes code localization from simple file finding into actionable diagnosis for repair agents. It helps LLM agents spend less time searching and more time making effective fixes by producing structured, repair-ready fault hypotheses.
problem_solved: LLM-based code repair agents often waste a large share of their budget on locating the bug before they can edit. Existing localization methods are usually evaluated as retrieval tasks, so they return locations without the diagnostic context needed for downstream repair.
method: Uses a training-free localization pipeline built around a reasoning LLM.
Pairs the LLM with compact repository representations to explore code systematically and form structured hypotheses about faults.
Outputs diagnostic, repair-relevant localization results rather than just file or line rankings.
impact: For practitioners building code agents, SHERLOC can improve efficiency by reducing wasted search effort and giving the repair model better starting information. This can lead to faster, more targeted bug fixes in repository-scale tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing locate -> diagnose -> repair flow
Split-screen comparison of retrieval-only localization vs SHERLOC diagnostic output
Repository heatmap or annotated code file highlighting suspected fault regions
Icon set for search, reasoning, bug, and fix to show agent workflow
paper_title: SHERLOC: Structured Diagnostic Localization for Code Repair Agents
paper_authors: Hovhannes Tamoyan, Sean Narenthiran, Erik Arakelyan, Mira Mezini, Boris Ginsburg
